comparison: Both address the core PTE findings showing AI-to-DMN/FPN information flow (C2-C4, C30-C45, C50-C51, C57). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED with strong statistical evidence. Peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the findings as 'valuable' and 'convincing' but expressing significant concern that the directed information flow may reflect general attentional/cognitive demands rather than memory-specific processes, especially given the lack of relationship to task performance.

Perfect agreement on high-gamma suppression findings (C6, C21-C29). Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights statistical support and replication across experiments. Peer reviewers do not raise specific concerns, with the editor describing findings as 'valuable' and analyses as 'convincing,' and the reviewer praising replication across task contexts.

Both address IFG control analyses (C5, C48-C49) and agree these are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the inverse pattern in IFG and significantly higher net outflow from AI as strengthening AI's unique role. Peer reviewers do not challenge these control analyses, with the editor describing overall analyses as 'convincing.'

Strong disagreement on the null finding regarding memory performance (C52). OpenEval rates this SUPPORTED as an appropriately reported negative result. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN and explicitly highlight this as a major concern, using the lack of relationship to memory performance as key evidence that the findings may not be memory-specific but rather reflect general cognitive demands.

Perfect agreement on PLV null findings (C58-C59). Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval interprets these as justifying the PTE analytical approach. Peer reviewers do not challenge the PLV findings or methodological choice of PTE, with preprocessing and connectivity analysis described as 'sensible and appropriate based on field standards.'

Both address dataset and methodological descriptions (C8, C60-C61, C65-C66, C73-C75) and agree these are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes substantial sample size and appropriate electrode coverage. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the dataset, with the editor commending 'the use of a large intracranial EEG dataset' and the reviewer calling the sample 'impressively-sized' and praising the replication approach.

Strong agreement on methodological justifications (C62-C64, C76-C79, C100-C103). Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights appropriate citations and empirical validation of analytical choices. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'Preprocessing of iEEG data also seems sensible and appropriate based on field standards,' encompassing the PTE methodology and justification.

Both address limitations and interpretations (C87-C88, C90, C92), but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates these SUPPORTED as appropriate acknowledgments of limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, directly challenging memory-specificity and emphasizing findings may reflect 'on-task cognition in general (though, perhaps not specific to memory),' while noting the authors 'have thoughtfully noted in the Discussion several ways that experimental design can be improved.'

Both address the study's main conclusions (C104-C106). OpenEval rates these SUPPORTED as meaningful advances extending the triple network model to episodic memory. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether findings truly arise from memory-associated processes versus general attentional/cognitive demands, though acknowledging the findings provide 'intriguing information about the structure and order of communication between network regions.'

OpenEval evaluates theoretical framework claims (C1, C9-C18) as SUPPORTED, noting they establish well-established concepts with extensive citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers do not challenge the theoretical foundation.

OpenEval evaluates high-gamma background claims (C19-C20, C80-C81) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers do not dispute these established properties.

OpenEval evaluates interpretations of high-gamma findings (C82-C86) as SUPPORTED, noting they are reasonable given the data though somewhat speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific interpretive claims.

OpenEval evaluates theoretical connections to controllability theory and Atkinson-Shiffrin model (C93-C99) as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable extensions though speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these theoretical frameworks.
